name: insimul-unreal-tooling
comment: `check` is the toolchain-free gate — a structural scan, the corpus manifest,
and the band-120 mechanic host manifest (every host interface core's module
manifest names is mirrored, member for member, and implemented or stubbed with
a stated consequence). `check:host` compiles the PORTABLE slice of the runtime
module and runs it against the golden fixtures; it needs only cmake and a C++17
compiler (no Unreal, no UBT), so the merge gate runs it too. It drops the
libinsimulcore legs with a configure-time WARNING when no native build is
beside it — read that warning rather than the pass count.
`check:host:binaries` is the same suite with -DINSIMUL_REQUIRE_BINARIES=ON, so
that warning becomes a hard failure: it is this harness's --require-binaries,
and it is what proves an adoption claim rather than assuming one. It adds the
three bridge-linked legs — radiant_bridge, quest_parity_core and (146 US-1)
mechanic_bridge, which asks the shipped libinsimulcore `core.methods` and pins
the answer so a mechanic row ARRIVING fails as loudly as one disappearing.

scripts.check: node verify-unreal/check.mjs && node vendor-conformance.mjs --check && node verify-mechanics/check-mechanics.mjs
scripts.check:host: cmake -S verify-unreal -B verify-unreal/build && cmake --build verify-unreal/build && ctest --test-dir verify-unreal/build --output-on-failure
scripts.check:host:binaries: cmake -S verify-unreal -B verify-unreal/build -DINSIMUL_REQUIRE_BINARIES=ON && cmake --build verify-unreal/build && ctest --test-dir verify-unreal/build --output-on-failure
scripts.check:full: npm run check && npm run check:host:binaries
